title: From cells to organ systems
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The closest bank point covers only the levels of organisation from cells to organ systems, but the new point also asks students to link each cell's shape to its job, which the bank point does not teach, so no single bank point matches it exactly.

draft.title: From cells to organ systems
card: Cells in many living things are specialised. Each type has a shape that suits its job.
long and thin, so it can carry signals over a distance.
has a thin extension that reaches out into the soil. This gives a large surface to take in water.

A group of similar cells doing the same job is a tissue. Different tissues working together make an organ, such as the heart. Organs working together make an organ system, such as the circulatory system.
draft.remember: Cells make tissues, tissues make organs, organs make systems, and a cell's shape suits its job.

a.q: Which list shows the levels of organisation in order, from smallest to largest?
a.why: Similar cells form a tissue, tissues form an organ, and organs form an organ system. Cell, organ, tissue is tempting but wrong, because an organ is made of several tissues, so tissue comes before organ.
a.clue: Start with the smallest unit, the cell.

b.q: Mia looks at a plant root under a microscope. The cells near the tip have thin extensions that reach into the soil. Why does this shape suit their job?
opts: It gives a large surface to take in water
It lets the cell carry signals over a distance
It lets the cell make sugars from sunlight
It lets the cell join with others to form an organ
b.why: A thin extension spreads the cell out into the soil, so there is a large surface for water to enter. Carrying signals over a distance is the job of a long, thin nerve cell, not a root hair cell.
b.clue: Think about what a root takes from the soil.

wants.brief: Two labelled cells side by side: a nerve cell, long and thin with branched ends, and a root hair cell with a thin extension reaching into soil.
wants.why: Seeing both shapes helps students link each shape to its job.

b.best: It gives a large surface to take in water
